title: resolve operator reconciliation loop caused by secret-merge order change during on-prem upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: After the 2026.02 operator/helm chart rollout to Private/VPC customers, several customers reported tenant-specific API failures and repeated operator reconcile churn. Investigation shows the operator entered a deterministic reconciliation loop for tenants where external secret rotation happened during the upgrade. The loop caused transient loss of in-flight manifest writes and left some tenant CRs with stale, partially-applied annotations which in some cases prevented autoscaler reconciliation and API initialization.

Scope: Affects ~6 Private tenants across two on-prem clusters (customer-reported). Not every tenant hit the failure; pattern correlates with clusters that have external-secret rotation immediately following Helm post-upgrade hooks. Hosted and Dedicated (Redwood-managed) were not impacted.

Observed behavior: operator pod log showed repeated "merge conflict" style warnings for tenant configs and kept reapplying the same patch set every 7s. Some tenants reported increased 5xx rates from the control-plane shim (10-30% for a 15–30 minute window) and delayed token provisioning.

Root cause hypothesis: A change in Helm values overlay ordering (chart template refactor in operator-templates) changed the ordering of secret/ConfigMap creation relative to the post-install mutating webhook. When the cluster had an automated external-secret rotation immediately after upgrade, the operator's naive secret-merge routine (in applyTenantManifest) encountered resource versions that had moved under a different ownership path and retried without an idempotent merge strategy. The operator retried by re-issuing the same patch sequence which triggered the webhook, which mutated fields again and produced new resourceversions; this caused an infinite feedback loop between the operator's merge logic and the webhook's mutation logic.

Proof: Repro script created from a customer cluster capture reproduces the loop within a local Kind cluster when external-secret apply is triggered concurrently with the post-upgrade helm hook. We captured the operator trace logs and kube-apiserver audit logs showing the alternating update sequence and the same three fields flipping order.

Impact mitigation already deployed: 1) temporarily disabled post-upgrade webhook mutation for affected tenant namespaces via a safe annotation for 3 customers (manual mitigation coordinated with SEs). 2) Provided remediation script to reconcile stuck CRs (idempotent replace with preserved UID and status). 3) Customer-facing incident notes sent and dedicated escalation channel opened.

Proposed permanent fix: 1) Add idempotent secret-merge operator code path that performs a 3-way merge using last-applied, desired, and live content and uses optimistic compare-and-swap (resourceVersion) with exponential backoff. 2) Add preflight hook in Helm operator chart that asserts no external-secret rotation is in-progress (fail the upgrade or postpone) or provide a canary rollout flag to stage the webhook enablement. 3) Introduce a short-term reconcile-backoff wall for repeated identical diffs to prevent tight loops (operator self-throttle). 4) Add unit and e2e tests that reproduce simultaneous external-secret rotation + helm post-install mutation.

Acceptance criteria: - No reconcile loops reproduced in e2e harness. - Idempotent merge code passes property tests and reduces unnecessary writes by >95% in synthetic workload. - Automated preflight blocks upgrades when the cluster reports recent Secret change events in the target namespaces within a configurable window. - Rollout plan validated in staging and in one willing customer cluster before broad release.

Rollout plan: - Implement fix on feature branch and open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/PR-xx (link in comments). - Run e2e scenario in CI and a dedicated long-running stress job for 48h. - Release operator-2026.03.1 to canary customers (one customer that volunteered) with a support engineer present. - If green for 24h, release to remaining Private clusters with an automated preflight. - Post-release monitoring: add metric for "reconcile-loop-detected" and pager rule for >5 tenants within 15 min.

Communication: Draft customer notification for the 6 impacted tenants and standard postmortem template prepared. Engineering will coordinate with Solutions and Support for runbook updates.
